title: Jobcentre Calculator
welcome_lead: The Office for National Statistics needs your calculator. Crunch unemployment rates, claimant counts and labour force data.
meta_desc: GCSE Economics calculations adventure on unemployment: rate calculations, ILO vs claimant count and trends.
final_note: Numbers nailed. Stretch yourself in the exam finale!

concepts.def: Survey of those actively seeking work.
Not working AND not seeking work.

walkthroughs.body_html: Rate = unemployed ÷ labour force × 100. UK example: 1.4m unemployed, labour force 34m. Rate = 1.4/34 × 100 ≈ 4.1%. Note: only those actively seeking work count — full-time students and retirees are not in the labour force.
ILO (International Labour Organization): survey-based; counts everyone actively searching. Wider measure. Claimant count: only those on benefits. Narrower. Both used, ILO is the headline.
Unemployment falls from 1.6m to 1.4m. Absolute change: −0.2m. % change: (−0.2 / 1.6) × 100 = −12.5%. Always show your working — examiners reward method marks.
